image_prompt.text: A large rectangular lobby of dark cracked stone tiles, walled on four sides by tall dark weathered grey stone brick and capped by a low ceiling of dark decaying panels, the whole room in deep greys, blacks and dark browns so it reads abandoned and decayed
An old reception counter desk in dark worn wood standing at the centre of the lobby, the one large distinct structure that tells the player where they are the moment they step in
A clear walking route across the tiled floor running from the front-wall entrance, past the reception counter, to the exit at the back, so movement through the lobby has an obvious grain

Composed views built for the creepy atmosphere — the broken chandelier hanging over the reception counter seen from the entrance, the pillared corners falling away into darkness — each framed to look good from where a player naturally stands
A large entrance doorway on the front wall, a tall arched opening
An exit doorway on the back wall
Tall cracked stone pillars, one in each corner of the room
A broken chandelier hanging from the low ceiling above the centre of the lobby

layout_placement.text: Expose adjustable attributes for fog level, wall darkness and light intensity so the scary atmosphere can be tuned later

notes: Classified None, not Survival: the prompt describes a place, a palette and a mood, with no chase, killer, escape or resource loop. 'For a horror game' is the theme the room is dressed for, not a game type, so no-genre.md was loaded and no genre was invented to escape it.

Preset Explorable Place taken with the enclosure axis substituted to interior-only instead of the preset's default exterior — play happens entirely inside this one enclosed room. All three preset options (landmark-focal, path-circulation, vignette-photo) are kept, so the preset is still what is being built. interior-only carries no pipeline cost; only transition would, and there is no outside to step in from.

The floor, walls, ceiling, doorways, corner pillars and chandelier match no option row in the loaded file and are carried as free text in image_prompt so the room's specific materials and props survive.

The fog / wall-darkness / light-intensity request is not geometry but a set of tunable properties of it, so it is carried in layout_placement rather than dropped; if the pipeline has no attribute channel it should surface as a build note rather than be silently lost.
No Universal Option was used — nothing in the prompt asks for inhabitants, water, terrain relief, settlement density, islands, or a building entered from outside.

would have asked: Sounds like an environment showcase built as a single enclosed room — a focal reception desk at the centre, a clear walk from the arched front entrance to the back exit, and composed creepy views of the space, plus your four corner pillars, the broken chandelier and the decayed grey-black palette. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: is this room the whole build, or the front hall of a larger haunted place players carry on into? Taken as the whole build — one enclosed interior, single-pass, nothing generated separately. If corridors or rooms beyond the exit door are wanted, that becomes a different, slower build.

would have asked: do players spawn and gather in this lobby before a round? If so it would take an arrival point at the entrance and read as a Social Space rather than an Explorable Place; nothing in the prompt says so, so no spawn was placed.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
